quote: Not really interested right now, but
stewart_read: This is the textbook hello-objection trigger in the first 30 seconds, but rep never used the 'can I have 30 seconds' small-ask pattern — he jumped straight into pitch content instead.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the customer's tone as soft enough not to need the formal ask; but the customer's very next words confirm active disinterest, so the protocol was needed.
coaching_implication: Drill the small-ask response verbatim for the first-30-seconds not-interested trigger instead of freelancing into program explanation.

quote: Give me a ballpark figure on what it cost.
stewart_read: This is a scripted trigger phrase with a canonical redirect-to-design response; rep partially uses it but undercuts it by still volunteering tax-incentive mechanics.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically building trust by answering a little before redirecting — but he never completes the redirect into gathering info to book, so the concession wins out.
coaching_implication: Use the full redirect_to_design line and stop after it; don't let cost detail leak out before the appointment is set.

quote: I know you can sell the credits.
stewart_read: Rep responds to a tax-credit mechanics question with actual financial explanation ('you're paying nothing out of pocket') instead of the universal escape hatch.
coaching_implication: This is closer-tier content; redirect immediately with the escape-hatch line and move to scheduling.

quote: Can I reach you back at this number?
stewart_read: Customer offers a logistics-based deflection; rep never counters with a firm time anchor or alternative slot, letting the call drift toward an open-ended callback.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be reading the plumbing emergency as genuine and deferring out of politeness — reasonable in the moment, but he still should have tried to lock a specific day/time before hanging up.
coaching_implication: Even with a real interruption, close with 'What day next week works, morning or afternoon?' rather than leaving it fully open.

quote: I just I'll email you, in a week.
stewart_read: Call ends without any day/time, verbal handshake, or rep-owned next step — a textbook unanchored soft exit.
coaching_implication: Rep should have proposed a specific callback window ('I'll call you Tuesday at 10, does that work?') instead of accepting an open-ended email promise.

quote: I shot you a text. So you have my personal number and personal bank number
stewart_read: Rep gives out a personal number as a workaround for follow-up, the exact anti-pattern flagged for privacy/security review.
coaching_implication: Flag for security review; rep should use the standard company follow-up channel, not personal contact info.

quote: does the the government credit, does that pay for a lot of it?
stewart_read: Second instance of rep answering financial-mechanism questions directly rather than deferring to the closer, reinforcing the price-pressure pattern.
coaching_implication: Same escape-hatch redirect applies; repeated pattern suggests this needs explicit drilling, not a one-off note.
